html:
An English naturalist and botanist who sailed on James Cook's first voyage and later used his influence to push for a British colony in Australia.

Banks was rich and paid for his own team of naturalists and artists on the Endeavour, which left England in 1768. They visited Brazil, Tahiti and New Zealand, and in April 1770 they landed at a bay in eastern Australia that Cook named Botany Bay for the many new plants found there. Banks came home famous in 1771.

He was president of the Royal Society for more than 41 years and an adviser on the royal gardens at Kew, where he sent plant collectors around the world. In 1779 he told Parliament that Botany Bay would suit a penal colony, which led to the First Fleet of 1788. He backed the Bounty breadfruit voyage, managed King George III's merino flock, and helped bring merino sheep to the colony. The plant genus Banksia is named after him.
